prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
competitors_mentioned: Ohio State Univ. College of Dentistry
answer_verbatim:
I can’t authoritatively name a single “best” dentist for implants in Columbus—“best” depends on your anatomy, medical history, the complexity of the case, and whether you need bone grafting, extractions, sinus lifts, or a full-arch solution. That said, here’s how to find a top implant provider and what to ask so you get a high-quality result.

Who to look for
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): best for complex surgery, extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, IV sedation. Many are board-certified by the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (ABOMS).
- Periodontists: specialists in the supporting tissues (gums and bone) and commonly place implants; many are board-certified by the American Board of Periodontology.
- Prosthodontists: specialists in restoring teeth and designing implant crowns/bridges/overdentures; look to involve a prosthodontist if your case is complex or esthetic demands are high.
- Dentists with advanced implant training (AAID or ICOI credentials) can also be excellent for straightforward cases.

Where to search in Columbus
- University dental clinics (Ohio State Univ. College of Dentistry) — good for complex cases and multi-specialty treatment.
- Look for local clinics with combined teams (oral surgeon + restorative dentist/prosthodontist) so the surgical and crown parts are coordinated.
- Use professional directories: ABOMS.org, American Academy of Periodontology, American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), and state dental board lookup for licenses/disciplinary history.

What to verify
- Board certification or advanced specialty training (OMS, periodontist, prosthodontist).
- How many implants they place annually and success rates.
- Whether they use 3D CBCT imaging and guided implant planning.
- The implant systems they use (Straumann, Nobel, Zimmer, etc.) and why.
- Coordination between the surgeon and the restorative dentist.
- Before/after photos and patient references or reviews.
- Warranty/guarantee and follow-up protocol.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- Am I a candidate for an implant? If not, what alternatives?
- Do I need bone grafting or sinus lift? If so, how will that affect time and cost?
- Who will place the implant and who will make the crown? How do you coordinate?
- What implant system do you use and why?
- What sedation or anesthesia options do you offer?
- What are the total costs (surgery + implant + abutment + crown + any grafting)? What financing options exist?
- What are the risks, complications, and your complication management plan?

Price ballpark
- Single implant (surgery + implant + abutment + crown) in the U.S.: roughly $3,000–$6,000 on average. Simple cases can be lower; complex cases (grafts, sinus lifts, staged treatments) can be much higher. Get a written estimate.

Red flags
- Unwillingness to use 3D imaging for treatment planning when indicated.
- No clear restorative plan (surgery done without discussing the crown).
- Vague answers about experience or success rates.
- Extremely low cost with pressure to commit immediately.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer a specialist type (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist, or a general dentist who places implants), and I’ll compile a short list of highly rated local providers and how to verify them.
